name: Gilbert O'Sullivan
hook: An Irish singer-songwriter whose refusal to license a sample, and the court case that followed, changed how hip-hop was made.
blurb: Raymond 'Gilbert' O'Sullivan was born in Waterford, Ireland, in 1946 and grew up in Swindon, England. His 1972 song 'Alone Again (Naturally)' was number one in America for six weeks. His place on this map is entirely a lawsuit. In 1991 Biz Markie used a loop of its piano on his song 'Alone Again'. Biz had asked O'Sullivan's permission and been refused, and the record came out anyway. O'Sullivan objected to his song being used without his consent, sued, and won: Grand Upright Music v. Warner Bros. Records (1991). The court agreed that sampling without a licence was infringement, and from then on anyone sampling a record had to get permission first. That made a pop singer-songwriter far from hip-hop one of the people who most changed how hip-hop records were made.
